Hide Tanaka was born in Japan in 1956 and played 70’s rock & roll as a guitarist and bassist. His fascination with jazz led him to relocate to New York City in 1982 where he eventually established himself as a versatile acoustic bassist. He is a member of the Junior Mance Trio and appears on a number of recordings, including “Love at Café Loup” and “Out South.”
Hide was interviewed in Clinton, New York on April 3, 2014 by Monk Rowe, director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
My name is Monk Rowe and we are in the jazz archive room at Hamilton College, and I’m pleased to have Hide Tanaka here with me today, visiting with Junior Mance. Welcome.
You said the last interview you did was with Russian television?
Yeah. We had — Junior had a concert last October in Israel. We had like seven concerts.
